title: Signature Mechanized soundness in Coq/Lean
description: Signature edition: Paper soundness proofs have bugs; mechanized ones don't (modulo the spec). Mechanizing progress+preservation in Coq or Lean turns the soundness argument into checked code — language designers ship the proof with the language, and extensions re-check instead of re-argue.
method: Formalize syntax, semantics, typing; prove the lemmas with tactics; the kernel checks everything; CI re-checks on changes.
usage: Mechanize from the start for new languages; the proof guides the design (unprovable = badly designed).

demo.code:
print('Lean: 2,400 lines, progress + preservation for core calculus')
print('kernel: CHECKED — language extension re-verified in CI')

title: Signature Blame assignment in contracts
description: Signature edition: Higher-order contracts (like gradual types) need blame: when a contract fails deep inside a callback, who broke it? The blame theorem for contracts proves the blamed party is the one that violated the contract — contract monitoring you can trust to point fingers correctly.
method: Wrap values with contract monitors carrying blame labels; on violation, the label identifies the violator; prove blame correctness.
usage: Read blame labels in contract errors — they name the guilty module precisely.

demo.code:
print('contract violation: expected Int, got String')
print('blame: module "parser" (positive party) — fix there')

title: Signature Effect systems soundness
description: Signature edition: Effect systems track what code does (I/O, exceptions, state) in the types; soundness means the effects a program actually performs are within its declared effect set. Callers know exactly what a function can do — the type is an honest capability manifest.
method: Annotate with effect rows; check effect polymorphism; prove the actual effects ⊆ declared effects.
usage: Use effect types at API boundaries; let inference fill in the internals.

demo.code:
print('f : () -> Int with <read>')
print('f tries network write -> EFFECT ERROR (not in declared set)')

title: Signature Type inference soundness
description: Signature edition: Inference (Hindley-Milner) must be sound: the inferred type must actually hold. Soundness of inference means the algorithm never assigns a wrong type — principal types are correct types. The proof connects the algorithm to the declarative typing rules.
method: Prove the inference algorithm sound (inferred ⇒ derivable) and complete (derivable principal ⇒ inferred) w.r.t. the declarative system.
usage: Trust inferred types; when inference surprises you, the declarative rules explain why.

demo.code:
print('infer: map f [1,2] : List b (f : a -> b)')
print('soundness: inferred type derivable in declarative system -> TRUST')

title: Signature Soundness regression suites
description: Signature edition: Type systems evolve; soundness regressions are catastrophic (a hole in the type system undermines everything). Soundness regression suites collect tricky programs — one per known soundness bug class — and the typechecker must handle each correctly on every change.
method: Curate programs exercising soundness-critical corners; run on every typechecker change; any new acceptance of a bad program blocks the change.
usage: Add a case for every soundness bug ever found; treat the suite as the type system's immune system.

demo.code:
print('suite: 214 soundness-critical programs')
print('change #881: 214/214 handled correctly -> MERGE')

title: Signature Session types for protocols
description: Signature edition: Session types type communication protocols: send Int then receive Bool then close. Soundness means well-typed processes never deadlock or miscommunicate — the protocol the types describe is the protocol the program follows, proved statically.
method: Type channels with session types; check duality of endpoints; progress = communication never gets stuck on mismatched expectations.
usage: Use for critical protocol code; generate the session types from the protocol spec.

demo.code:
print('client: !Int.?Bool.end  server: ?Int.!Bool.end (dual)')
print('session check: DUAL -> communication sound')

title: Signature Soundness for gradual typing
description: Signature edition: Gradual typing mixes typed and untyped code with runtime casts; soundness means typed code can't be blamed for untyped code's errors (the blame theorem). Siek-Taha's blame calculus proves casts either succeed or blame the untyped boundary precisely — typed code is never at fault.
method: Insert casts at typed/untyped boundaries; prove the blame theorem: failed casts blame the less-typed side.
usage: Design gradual systems around blame; test that errors blame the dynamic side.

demo.code:
print('typed f calls untyped g; cast fails')
print('blame: g\'s boundary (untyped side) — typed code exonerated')

title: Signature Ownership and borrow checking (Rust)
description: Signature edition: Rust's borrow checker proves memory safety at compile time via ownership types: each value has one owner, borrows are tracked, and the borrowck verifies no use-after-free or data race can occur. It's type soundness extended to lifetimes — the most industrially successful soundness proof ever shipped.
method: Ownership types + lifetime inference; borrowck checks outlives relations; violations are compile errors, not runtime bugs.
usage: Trust the borrowck; when it complains, the design usually needs rethinking, not the checker.

demo.code:
print('let x = vec![1]; let r = &x; drop(x); use(r)')
print('borrowck: ERROR — use after move (soundness enforced at compile time)')
